newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia,Italy start economic cooperation agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia,Italy start economic cooperation agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia's largest commercial bank Beobanka and Italy's financial organisation Finest set up on Thursday an agency to promote economic cooperation between the two countries.
BeoFinest is to channel foreign investment to Serbia through joint ventures between Italian and Serbian firms.

"The aim is to find Italian entrepreneurs, small and medium companies with good growth potential, striving for internationalisation and opportunities in the region," Finest president Leonardo Simonelli said at a signing ceremony.
Simonelli said Finest wanted to invest in Serbia but the country urgently needed to restructure its economy and finances.
Finest has around 250 million German marks in capital to promote economic cooperation between north-eastern Italy and East European countries, he added.
"Financial resources are scarce and you have to compete for them," Simonelli said.
Apart from providing staff, Finest has also set aside two million dollars, one million each for feasibility studies and technical assistance.
Feasibility studies, to be prepared over next 1-1/2 years are needed for all Serbian companies who wished to compete for credit support by the Italian government and banks.
"Over the period, we want to see the acceptance, how useful it can be for this government to have joint venture between Finest and Beobanka," Simonelli said.

"We are also waiting to see the famous privatisation law. We saw the draft, made some comments and now wait to see the end product. Beside the (privatisation) law, other legal framework must be put in order," he told Reuters.
The new agency also wants to give support to privatisation ministry for small and medium enterprises.
Beobanka's general manager Zlatan Perucic said the bank, being a part of the joint venture, will scan various projects and offer them to Finest.

"It can be direct investment with Beobanka as a guarantor, joint investment with Finest providing part of an investment. But Finest also wants to take part in privatisation of small and medium enterprises," Perucic said.

Beobanka has around 27,000 clients, mostly small and medium enterprises from agriculture and processing industries. In order to qualify for financial support, each project must first get a go ahead from Beobanka.
"There are parts of agriculture and processing industry we wish to include in the project. Some of those are put on hold due to lack of funds," Perucic said.
Yugoslav Foreign Trade Minister Borislav Vukovic said Belgrade was offering numerous benefits to investors.
"Italian investors are offered a good treatment. There will be import relaxation for purchasing equipment, free repatriation of profit and profit tax relief," he said.
With the exception of military industry, media and mass telecommunications, foreigners were allowed to obtain majority stake in Yugoslav companies in any other industry, he added.
Beside acquiring stake in local companies, foreigners can compete for concessions, invest in free trade zones, establish joint banks, Vukovic said.
But despite its readyness to invest, Finest may face obstacles in channeling international funds to Serbia.

Simonelli insisted Yugoslavia first needed to be accepted by the Bank of International Settlements (BIS), the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
"These are the three key international institutions helping transactions to this economy," Simonelli said. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
